sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Ashtabula County
sections.html:
In Jefferson, the auditor sets values and handles value disputes, and the treasurer mails bills and takes payment. The auditor works from the courthouse at 25 W Jefferson St, phone 440-576-3783. For the tax bill itself, a payoff amount on a sale or a delinquent balance, ask the Ashtabula County treasurer.

The county sits in Ohio's northeastern corner, and Jefferson is the county seat. The 2020 census counted 97,574 residents and 46,237 housing units, of which 14.9% were vacant. Among occupied homes, 71.0% were owner-occupied.

The county covers 1,368 square miles, 49% of it Lake Erie water. Three cities (Ashtabula, Conneaut and Geneva) sit beside seven villages: Andover, Geneva-on-the-Lake, Jefferson, North Kingsville, Orwell, Roaming Shores and Rock Creek. Lake-effect snow falls often, so roofs, gutters and drainage matter to buyers.

A house in a lakeside village and a farmhouse inland can sit in very different taxing districts. The parcel number on your bill is the starting point for every question below.

sections.h2: How to challenge your property value
sections.html:
Valuation complaints are taken from January 1 through March 31, filed with the auditor for the Board of Revision. The statute, ORC 5715.19(A)(1), actually lets a complaint arrive up to the later of March 31 of the ensuing year or the day first-half collection closes. A mailed complaint is dated by its postal postmark. Metered postage from a private machine does not count.

The Board adjusts values, not tax dollars. The burden of proof sits with the person filing, so bring paperwork:

  • A closing statement and contract from a recent purchase.
  • An independent appraisal.
  • Repair estimates for defects in the house.
  • Rent and expense statements for an income property.

Two arguments carry no weight: how fast your tax grew, and how your value compares with a nearby parcel. Paper forms go to the auditor's office, and e-filed forms go to bor@ashtabulacounty.gov. The Board of Revision phone line is 440-576-1484, staffed weekdays from eight until half past four.

Expect a certified-mail notice of the hearing date at least ten days ahead. The Board has 180 days, counted from the last filing day, to rule. If you disagree with the decision, you have 30 days, counted from the postmark on the decision letter, to appeal. You can go to the state Board of Tax Appeals in Columbus or to the Court of Common Pleas in Jefferson, and the notice of appeal goes to the Board of Revision and the forum you choose.

Two more rules from ORC 5715.19 affect timing:

  • While a complaint is open, you can pay tax computed on your claimed value, and the treasurer has to take it.
  • A final value above your claim means interest on the gap, dated back to the original due date.
  • Hold nothing back. Evidence you keep from the Board can be shut out of any later appeal.

Usually not right away. Once a parcel has a complaint, subsection (A)(2) of the same statute bars more complaints through the rest of that interim period unless circumstances changed after the lien date. The exceptions are an arm's-length sale, casualty loss, a substantial improvement, or a change of at least fifteen percent in occupancy that hurts the property economically.

A school board or other party may answer a large request with a counter-complaint, and the threshold is $17,500 in taxable value.

sections.h2: Key dates and rules for sellers
sections.html:
Ohio rules that apply to an Ashtabula County sale
TopicRule
Complaint windowJanuary 1 through March 31
Appeal after decision30 days after the letter's postmark
Hearing noticeAt least ten days ahead, by certified mail
Standard payment datesAll by December 31, or half then and half by June 20
Deed transfer fee$1 minimum, or 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction, if higher

The statute sets the general schedule, so ask the Ashtabula County treasurer for the dates printed on your own bill.

sections.h2: What the auditor charges on transfer
sections.html:
ORC 319.54(G)(3) lets the auditor collect $1, or 10 cents per $100 of value (a fraction counts as a full $100), whichever is higher. The seller pays it. If the commissioners have levied a Chapter 322 transfer tax, that comes on top, so ask the auditor whether Ashtabula County has one.

The buyer files a value statement with it. Under ORC 319.202 that form records the seller's answers about a homestead or owner-occupancy tax reduction and about farm-use valuation, and farmland that drops out of the program can face a recoupment charge. Gifts between spouses or between parent and child are exempt, as are transfers on a sale for delinquent taxes.

Get a payoff number from the treasurer before a contract is signed. Back taxes turn up in the title search and are usually paid from what the seller receives at closing. If a value complaint is pending, tell the title company, because the amount due may be set by the tender rule above.

Vacant houses, roofs worn down by lake-effect winters and parcels with back taxes can still sell as-is, and the same payoff steps apply. Pull the parcel record from the auditor first so acreage and building details match your deed.

A cash buyer does not change the order of things. You still need the payoff, the transfer fee and the value statement. What a cash sale removes is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the closing date depends mostly on how fast the treasurer and auditor answer you.

faqs.q: When can I file a property value complaint in Ashtabula County?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. The statute allows a later cutoff if first-half collection closes after March 31, and mail is dated by postmark.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about an Ashtabula County tax bill?
faqs.a: The treasurer answers for bills and payments. For values and exemptions, the auditor is at 440-576-3783, and the Board of Revision line is 440-576-1484.

faqs.q: Does the Board of Revision lower my tax bill?
faqs.a: It changes the value, and the tax follows from that. The Board adjusts values, not tax dollars, and it ignores how much your taxes rose or what a neighbor's parcel is valued at.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Board of Revision decision?
faqs.a: Yes, for 30 days after the postmark on the decision letter. Pick the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals in Columbus or the Court of Common Pleas in Jefferson, and send the notice to the Board of Revision too.

faqs.q: How much is the auditor's transfer charge?
faqs.a: At least $1, and 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction when that is more, under ORC 319.54(G)(3). The seller pays it, along with any county transfer tax. Ask the auditor whether Ashtabula County levies one.
